title: Preferred Stimulation Levels in Introverts and Extraverts: Effects on Arousal and Performance
research_question: How do preferred stimulation levels in introverts and extraverts affect psychophysiological arousal and paired-associates learning performance?

participants.description: Male undergraduate students from the University of Missouri, Columbia. 60 in Experiment 1 (30 extraverts, 30 introverts), 80 in Experiment 2 (40 extraverts, 40 introverts). Selected from upper and lower 25% on the E scale of the Eysenck Personality Inventory (EPI). Neuroticism (N) scores were controlled.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Recorded white noise delivered in random 1-second bursts with a mean interval of 10 seconds via stereo earphones. Intensity levels were controlled by a dial (0-100 units).
Paired-associates (PA) learning task: 14 S-R terms designed for high response interference, presented via photoslides.

measures.instrument: Dial setting (0-100 units) on tape recorder volume control switch
Skin conductance (maximum, minimum, spontaneous skin resistance responses - SRRs), Finger pulse volume (average, percentage change), Pulse rate (bpm)
Trials to criterion (two successive errorless trials)

findings.antecedent: Personality (Extravert vs. Introvert)
findings.mechanism: Extraverts are less excitable/arousable and seek higher stimulation to reach optimal arousal.
findings.quote: extraverts chose a higher level of intensity for the bursts of noise they received than did introverts.

findings.antecedent: Noise treatment (Choice vs. Assigned-Same for same personality type)
findings.mechanism: The mere fact of making a choice did not affect PR.
findings.quote: PR in each of the assigned-same conditions did not differ from that in the appropriate choice condition.

findings.antecedent: Personality (Introvert vs. Extravert) in assigned conditions (Experiment 1)
findings.mechanism: Introverts are more excitable/arousable than extraverts in response to given stimulation levels.
findings.quote: introverts showed higher pulse rates than extraverts.

findings.antecedent: Noise intensity (Introvert-chosen vs. Extravert-chosen) in assigned conditions (Experiment 1)
findings.mechanism: Higher stimulation intensity leads to higher arousal.
findings.quote: noise intensity, F(1, 36) = 9.90, p < .01.

findings.antecedent: Personality (Introvert vs. Extravert) stimulated at noise level chosen by their own personality type (Experiment 1)
findings.mechanism: When introverts and extraverts select their preferred stimulation levels, they achieve comparable optimal arousal.
findings.quote: As long as introverts and extraverts received noise at a level equal to that chosen by members of the same respective type, they showed equal rates.

findings.antecedent: Noise treatment or Personality (Experiment 1)
findings.quote: The measure of finger pulse volume did not show any significant effects during either baseline or treatment periods.

findings.antecedent: Noise treatment (Choice vs. Assigned-Same for same personality type)
findings.mechanism: The mere fact of making a choice did not affect SRRs.
findings.quote: The assigned-same condition did not differ from the choice condition.

findings.antecedent: Personality (Introvert vs. Extravert) in assigned conditions (Experiment 1)
findings.mechanism: Introverts are more excitable/arousable than extraverts in response to given stimulation levels.
findings.quote: introverts show evidence of greater arousal than extraverts.

findings.antecedent: Noise intensity (Introvert-chosen vs. Extravert-chosen) in assigned conditions (Experiment 1)
findings.mechanism: Higher stimulation intensity leads to higher arousal.
findings.quote: noise intensity, F(1, 36) = 6.32, p < .05.

findings.antecedent: Personality (Introvert vs. Extravert) stimulated at noise level chosen by their own personality type (Experiment 1)
findings.mechanism: When introverts and extraverts select their preferred stimulation levels, they achieve comparable optimal arousal.
findings.quote: Introverts and extraverts receiving stimulation at a level chosen by members of similar personality type showed equal numbers of SRRs.

findings.antecedent: Noise treatment (Choice vs. Assigned-Same for same personality type)
findings.mechanism: The mere fact of choice did not influence performance.
findings.quote: the mere fact of choice did not influence performance—subjects who were assigned noise equal in intensity to that chosen by their yoked counterparts in the assigned-same conditions performed as well as the latter.

findings.antecedent: Personality (Introvert vs. Extravert) x Noise intensity (Introvert-chosen vs. Extravert-chosen) interaction (Experiment 1)
findings.mechanism: Performance is optimal at preferred arousal levels, and deviations lead to impairment, differentially for introverts and extraverts.
findings.quote: An ANOVA showed a significant interaction between E-I and noise intensity level, F(1, 36) = 10.64, p < .01.

findings.antecedent: Introverts stimulated at noise level preferred by extraverts (higher intensity) (Experiment 1)
findings.mechanism: Overstimulation for introverts leads to poorer performance (over-arousal).
findings.quote: Introverts performed significantly less well than extraverts when stimulated at a level preferred by extraverts

findings.antecedent: Extraverts stimulated at noise level preferred by introverts (lower intensity) (Experiment 1)
findings.mechanism: Suboptimal stimulation for extraverts did not significantly impair performance.
findings.quote: extraverts did not differ from introverts when stimulated at a level preferred by introverts.

findings.antecedent: Introverts and Extraverts stimulated at levels chosen by their own personality type (Experiment 1)
findings.mechanism: Optimal arousal levels, achieved through self-selected stimulation, lead to comparable performance.
findings.quote: Under these conditions introverts and extraverts performed equally well.

findings.antecedent: Personality (Extravert vs. Introvert)
findings.mechanism: Extraverts prefer higher stimulation levels than introverts to reach their optimal arousal.
findings.quote: The mean noise intensity setting chosen was 50.4 and that of introverts 31.1. The difference between the two means was significant

findings.antecedent: Introverts' chosen lowest acceptable noise intensity vs. optimal noise intensity (Experiment 2)
findings.mechanism: Introverts have a lower threshold for acceptable stimulation.
findings.quote: The lowest acceptable intensity setting chosen by introverts was 21.1, which was significantly lower than 31.1

findings.antecedent: Extraverts' chosen highest acceptable noise intensity vs. optimal noise intensity (Experiment 2)
findings.mechanism: Extraverts have a higher threshold for acceptable stimulation.
findings.quote: The highest acceptable setting chosen by extraverts was 57.5, which was significantly higher than 50.4

findings.antecedent: Personality (Introvert vs. Extravert) x Noise intensity (Low, Mod-low, Mod-high, High) interaction (Experiment 2)
findings.mechanism: The relationship between noise intensity and arousal differs for introverts and extraverts.
findings.quote: the interaction between the two, F(3, 72) = 2.76, p < .05.

findings.antecedent: Personality (Introvert vs. Extravert) (Experiment 2)
findings.mechanism: Introverts are generally more aroused than extraverts at given stimulation levels.
findings.quote: significant effects for E-I, F(1, 72) = 15.50, p < .01

findings.antecedent: Noise intensity (Low, Mod-low, Mod-high, High) (Experiment 2)
findings.mechanism: Higher stimulation intensity leads to higher arousal.
findings.quote: the level of noise intensity, F(3, 72) = 17.98, p < .01

findings.antecedent: Personality (Introvert vs. Extravert) at most intense (High) and least intense (Low) noise levels (Experiment 2)
findings.mechanism: Arousal may be a curvilinear function of stimulation, with differences between E-I becoming nonsignificant at extreme levels.
findings.quote: introverts were equal to extraverts in PR in response to both the most intense and least intense level of noise

findings.antecedent: Personality (Introvert vs. Extravert) at intermediate (Mod-low, Mod-high) noise levels (Experiment 2)
findings.mechanism: Introverts are more aroused than extraverts at moderate stimulation levels.
findings.quote: introverts showed higher PR in response to both of the intermediate levels of noise.

findings.antecedent: Noise intensity (Low, Mod-low, Mod-high, High) (Experiment 2)
findings.mechanism: Performance follows an inverted-U relationship with arousal, which is modulated by noise intensity.
findings.quote: significant effects for noise intensity, F(3, 72) = 4.68, p < .01

findings.antecedent: Personality (Introvert vs. Extravert) x Noise intensity (Low, Mod-low, Mod-high, High) interaction (Experiment 2)
findings.mechanism: The optimal arousal level for performance differs between introverts and extraverts.
findings.quote: the interaction of noise intensity with E-I, F(3, 72) = 8.29; p < .01.

findings.antecedent: Introverts at Mod-low noise (their optimal) vs. Extraverts at Mod-high noise (their optimal) (Experiment 2)
findings.mechanism: Performance is best when stimulation is at the individual's optimal arousal level.
findings.quote: Both introverts and extraverts required fewer trials to reach criterion when stimulated at an intensity level chosen by each of them.

findings.antecedent: Introverts stimulated by noise at Mod-high or High levels (above their optimal) (Experiment 2)
findings.mechanism: Overstimulation leads to impaired performance for introverts.
findings.quote: Introverts showed poorer performance when stimulated by noise at the two higher levels of intensity

findings.antecedent: Extraverts stimulated by noise at Low or Mod-low levels (below their optimal) (Experiment 2)
findings.mechanism: Suboptimal stimulation leads to impaired performance for extraverts.
findings.quote: extraverts, however, showed a decrement in performance with deviations from the optimal level in both an upward and downward direction.

findings.antecedent: Introverts stimulated at Low noise level (below their optimal) (Experiment 2)
findings.mechanism: Introverts can function well at very low stimulation levels without significant impairment.
findings.quote: no significant decrement when stimulated at a level below their optimal level.

mechanisms: Eysenck's theory: Extraverts are less excitable/arousable than introverts due to different thresholds in the ascending reticular activating system (ARAS) and cortical/limbic centers. This leads to introverts being more aroused by given stimulation and having a lower optimal arousal level.
Yerkes-Dodson Law: An inverted-U relationship exists between arousal and performance, where optimal performance occurs at moderate arousal levels.

Easterbrook's Cue Utilization: Increased arousal narrows the range of cues utilized in problem solving. Initially, this eliminates distracting cues, improving performance. Beyond an optimal point, it eliminates central cues, impairing performance.
implementation_implications: To optimize paired-associates learning performance for both introverts and extraverts, stimulation should be provided at their respective optimal levels of intensity.

tables.description: Mean Trials to Criterion (Experiment 1) for Extraverts and Introverts under Choice, Assigned Introvert Choice, and Assigned Extravert Choice noise treatments.
Mean Trials to Criterion (Experiment 2) for Extraverts and Introverts under Low, Mod-low, Mod-high, and High noise conditions.

limitations: Experiment 1 could not draw conclusions about introverts at suboptimal stimulation or extraverts at superoptimal stimulation.
Conductance data in Experiment 2 was collected for only slightly more than half the subjects due to apparatus malfunction.
Cue utilization is only one possible explanation for the findings; arousal may also influence memory through its effects on retrieval and rehearsal.
Future research should focus on differences in impulsivity rather than solely E-I, as impulsivity may be the critical variable linking E-I to individual differences in arousability.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Introverts have higher baseline cortical arousal and prefer lower levels of external stimulation, while extraverts have lower baseline arousal and prefer higher levels of external stimulation to achieve optimal performance and arousal.

mechanism_chain.description: Personality differences (introversion/extraversion) influence baseline cortical arousal, leading to different preferred levels of external stimulation to maintain optimal arousal, which in turn affects actual arousal levels and cognitive performance.
